solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Obscures one source of malpractice in English county

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the abbreviated county name

parts.note: Beds is the standard short form of Bedfordshire
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so its opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of malpractice

explanation.surface: Someone is covering up wrongdoing somewhere in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedim is to make dim, so it obscures; both are third-person verbs.

clue.text: A cricket club in pub, at card game

indicators.note: in puts the letters inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A cricket team sits in the pub, playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game played against the banker.

clue.text: Caviar, for example, Cecil Day devoured

indicators.note: devoured suggests the name is chewed up, so its letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Cecil Day has wolfed down the caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Day is a made-up name; its letters supply the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is a classic example of a rare, choice food, a delicacy.

clue.text: Greek character s-scarpered, wrapped in scarf?

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the stammered s-scarpered tells us to stammer the word for scarpered, fled, giving f-fled

explanation.surface: A Greek character stammers that someone ran off, bundled up in a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in s-scarpered models a stutter, so FLED (scarpered, British slang for ran away) is stammered as F-FLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Muffled means wrapped up warmly, as a face in a muffler or scarf.

clue.text: Cuts back firm plasterwork

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word Cuts from its end to its start

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm is cutting back on its plastering work.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and mould decoration.

clue.text: Note kitty's been raised: it's understood

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
a kitty is a cat

explanation.surface: A note says the cat has been lifted up, and it is understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being said, understood silently.

clue.text: Hint that's left in something needed by Potter

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the stick a player uses

parts.note: a potter in snooker pots balls, and needs a cue to do it

explanation.surface: A hint is left inside something a pottery maker needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter suggests a pottery maker or Harry Potter, but it is a snooker player who pots balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint that points towards the solution.

clue.text: Put out books about America

indicators.note: about means the first letters go round the second

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone has published books about America.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to drive out or expel, to put someone out of a position.

clue.text: Regularly ice-cold English female, one seen on the staff

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of ice-cold, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: alternate letters of ice-cold

explanation.surface: A frosty Englishwoman is spotted among the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff here is the musical stave, not a workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: The C clef is a symbol placed on the musical stave to fix where middle C sits.

clue.text: In charge of trophies, after initially having minor problems

indicators.note: after places IC and CUPS following the single letter
initially points to the first letter of the word having

parts.note: first letter of having
cups are trophies awarded to winners

explanation.surface: Someone running the trophy cabinet is having small setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccups are small hitches or setbacks, an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Loud preacher has nearly half of Harvard university consumed by rage

indicators.note: Harvard has seven letters, so half is three and a half; nearly half takes its first three

parts.note: the first three letters of Harvard

indicators.note: consumed by puts the letter inside the word for rage

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: A shouting preacher is furious about Harvard university.
explanation.definitionFit: A haranguer delivers a long, loud, ranting speech, like a hectoring preacher.

clue.text: Get faster account, and celebrate, having lost heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of celebrate drops out

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to open a faster account and celebrate, but feels dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of CELEBRATE is its fifth letter B; removing it leaves CELERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to gain speed, to go more quickly.

clue.text: Manages CD counts differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone counts their CDs in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a business or operation is to run or direct it.

clue.text: Ginger nuts for ducks

parts.note: ginger hair is red
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Ginger nut biscuits are being given to ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginger nut is a British biscuit, which disguises the two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The redhead is a North American diving duck with a reddish head.

clue.text: One had, in manner of speaking and lying, to be clumsy?

indicators.note: in puts the contracted words inside the word for a way of speaking

parts.note: an accent is a manner of speaking
I'd is short for I had, with one standing for I
prone means lying face down

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, in their way of talking while lying down, to being awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accident-prone keeps having mishaps, which the question mark ties loosely to being clumsy.

clue.text: Revolutionary advice for holding dual gets approval

indicators.note: revolutionary means the whole thing is turned round, read backwards up the grid
holding puts the word dual inside the word for advice

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Radical advice on duality wins praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary here means turning round, not radical: the whole combination is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval.

clue.text: Handouts arranged by Thursday — but way down the list!

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Handouts are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Handouts are being sorted by Thursday, though the task is a low priority.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed thousandth in order sits very far down any ranking.

clue.text: Kicks poor journalists

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a verb, to kick roughly at the shins
second meaning: mediocre writers churning out copy

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out at struggling reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack covers both a rough kick at someone's legs and a writer of low-grade journalism.

clue.text: Live to the north of a region

indicators.note: to the north of places the first word above the letter in a down entry

parts.note: to be is to live or exist, and are is a form of be

explanation.surface: People dwell north of some region.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district of land.

clue.text: Necklace found in motor club

indicators.note: found in says the answer is sitting inside the words motor club

explanation.surface: A necklace has turned up at a motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Core RUC reforms take place again

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: The core of the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the old Northern Ireland police, is restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: To reoccur is to happen once more, to recur.

clue.text: Returning in lilac Cadillac, see old Asian capital

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words lilac Cadillac

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone drives back in a pale purple luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it signals the hidden word. A see is a bishop's seat; Dacca, now spelt Dhaka, is the Bangladeshi capital and a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacca is the older spelling of Dhaka, a diocesan city and the capital of Bangladesh.

clue.text: A cent — price for buttonhole?

parts.note: the cost of something is its price

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a single cent is the price of a flower for the lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttonhole looks like a flower for a lapel, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to stop and detain them in conversation, approaching them boldly.

clue.text: Old secret police force's lack of action

parts.note: the Stasi was East Germany's secret police
the possessive ending supplies a final S

explanation.surface: A defunct secret police force has become inactive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stagnation where nothing moves or changes.
